title: IT Act s. 56 — Income from other sources (Residuary head) (IT Act s. 56)

content.overview: Section 56 charges income from other sources, the residuary head. It includes dividends not taxed elsewhere, interest, winnings from lotteries and similar prizes, gifts of money or property above the enacted threshold from a non-relative, and other receipts that are income but not chargeable under an earlier head. Deductions are limited to the expenditure laid out to earn the income, other than the disallowances. Other sources is not a choice. It applies when no specific head does, and it also charges the items the section deems.

cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Other sources is not a choice. It applies when no specific head does, and it also charges the items the section deems.
essentialIngredients: Income not chargeable under another head, or a deemed item
Gift threshold and relative exclusion if a gift
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 56(1) is residuary. Section 56(2) deems specified receipts, including winnings, machinery let out, and gifts of money or specified property exceeding the enacted sum, with exclusions for relatives, marriage and inheritance. The gift figure is statutory and is not frozen here. A salary or rent does not move to this head because the taxpayer prefers it.
examples: Interest on a personal fixed deposit is other sources.
A gift from a friend above the threshold is tested under section 56(2).
A gift from a parent is checked against the relative exclusion.
